text:
Sophie (oncall): Hey team, getting multiple escalations — embeddings endpoint returning dimension-mismatch errors for some customers and elevated 5xx rate. Looks correlated with the 03:00 UTC model rollout. Anyone else seeing this?

Maria (support): Yep, two customers just opened tickets: one sees `400: embedding dimension mismatch (expected 1536, got 1024)`, the other is getting intermittent 502s when submitting batched requests. Both started ~03:07.

Alex (prod): I can confirm. Traffic spike ~03:05 when new variant `x-embed-aleph-v2` rolled to canary -> then promoted. Metrics: embedding success rate dropped from 99.9% -> 95% and the batch queue depth doubled.

Ben (infra): Pulling logs from the embedding workers now. Seen repeated error: 
```
ERROR [embed-worker] model=x-embed-aleph-v2 request_id=rid-8b2 dimension_check failed expected=1536 got=1024
WARN [batcher] queue_len=578 processing_time_ms=1200 backpressure=true
```
Katy (sre): Also saw sustained swap usage rise on the inference nodes around same time (possible quantized variant causing memory pressure and blocking).

Sophie (oncall): Action plan: 1) roll back to previous model variant for all traffic 2) open hotfix to validate dims server-side and return a clearer error 3) throttle noisy clients if necessary. I'll kick rollback now.

deploy-bot: started deployment rollback of deployment `embed-service:canary` -> `embed-service:stable` (initiated by Sophie).

Alex (prod): Rolling back now. Canary -> stable rollback in progress, expected 90s. Routing back to `x-embed-aleph-v1`.

Maria (support): I'll tell the affected customers we're rolling back and ask for recent request IDs so we can tie logs. Customer A gave a sample request id `rid-8b2`.

Ben (infra): After rollback, success rate creeping back up. But I'm still seeing a subset of workers with queued requests linger (some timeouts). Might be leftover queue built-up. I'm increasing processing threads temporarily on those nodes and clearing the internal batch queue.

Sophie (oncall): Can we get a quick repro from the customer that hit dimension mismatch? Maria, any sample payload?

Maria (support): Customer sent this curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"x-embed-aleph-v2","input":["foo","bar"]}'
```
Response: `400 {"error":"embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024"}`

Alex (prod): That confirms the model variant produced 1024-length vectors. Looks like v2 changed output dim (maybe accidentally switched to a smaller base or a different architecture).

Katy (sre): For customers hit by 502s, I checked gateway logs: downstream workers returned `upstream prematurely closed connection` during heavy batching windows. Probably memory thrash + longer per-batch latency -> gateway cut connection.

Sophie (oncall): Status update after rollback: success rate back to 99.8%, errors for that request_id no longer reproduce against stable. Customers still seeing sporadic 5xx?

Ben (infra): Reduced but a few nodes still report slow processing times. Manual intervention cleared most. Will keep an eye.

Alex (prod): Root cause hypothesis: promotion pipeline didn't validate embedding dimensionality across variants. `x-embed-aleph-v2` is a different architecture with 1024 dim but was treated as drop-in. That combined with kernel selection differences caused memory pressure under our batching heuristic.

Maria (support): Customers want a postmortem and timeline. Also asking for mitigation so they can avoid broken vectors in their index. Any short-term advice?

Sophie (oncall): Short-term: 1) pin model to `x-embed-aleph-v1` until we add compatibility checks 2) if you must use v2, include a client-side validation that checks vector length before ingesting to their index 3) we'll add a server-side validation that returns a deterministic error and an explicit header with expected dims.

Alex (prod): I'm opening a ticket to add a CI model compatibility check in the promotion pipeline that verifies embedding dimensions and a basic smoke test against a canonical prompt set. Also adding metrics alert for batcher queue length crossing 300 for >2m.

Katy (sre): Follow-up ops items: 1) add automated eviction for stuck batch queues 2) tune batching window to be adaptive to memory signals (if mem pressure -> shorten window) 3) add a canary traffic gate that keeps new architectures at 5% for 1h with dimension check.

Ben (infra): I'll schedule a rolling restart of nodes that showed high swap to ensure no leftover memory fragmentation.

Sophie (oncall): Final status: rollback successful, main customer tickets updated, interim mitigations in place. Creating incident postmortem and assigning owners.

Alex (prod): Incident ticket: INF-2026-874. Owning PRs: #4281 (compat check), #4282 (server-dim-validation), #4283 (batcher-alerts).

Maria (support): I'll follow up with customers with a timeline and the mitigation steps.

Katy (sre): Marking this thread as monitored for 2 hours; will escalate if queue lengths or 5xx rate climbs again. :eyes:

Sophie (oncall): Thanks everyone. Action items for postmortem: - root cause confirm (Alex) - CI gate + smoke tests (Alex) - server-side validation + clear error (Alex/Ben) - customer comms + timeline (Maria) - ops tuning + eviction (Katy/Ben).

Maria (support): Noted. Closing loop with customers now.

Sophie (oncall): I'll file the postmortem and ping on the channel when it's up.

deploy-bot: deployment rollback `embed-service` completed in 74s.

Katy (sre): Observability note: adding a dashboard tile for `embedding_vector_dim_mismatch_count` and `batcher_queue_depth` (new).

Sophie (oncall): Thread closed for now, will reopen if regressions surface.
